harnesses.name: Letta (agent framework, formerly MemGPT; the Letta agent harness, formerly Letta Code): subagents launched through the subagent (Task) tool (subagent_type, agent_id, background mode; fork built-in; memoryBlocks frontmatter)
harnesses.default_visibility: Assignment plus a selection of state: a fresh subagent with its own system prompt, tools and model, no parent conversation unless the fork built-in is chosen, and (for custom subagents) the memory blocks, since memoryBlocks defaults to all. 'The subagent runs autonomously with its own system prompt, tools, and model.' 'By default, the built-in subagents are not reused - they are created fresh on each invocation.' 'Which memory blocks the subagent can access: specific list, all, or none. Defaults to all.' The only built-in that carries the parent context is fork: 'Fork the parent conversation with full context and tools'. Returns: 'The final message from the subagent is returned to the main agent, which keeps the main agent's context clean.' In background mode: 'When the subagent finishes, a completion notification is automatically injected into the conversation, and the main agent can read the result.'
harnesses.quote: The subagent runs autonomously with its own system prompt, tools, and model.
harnesses.knob: subagent_type selects the built-in (fork: 'Fork the parent conversation with full context and tools'; general-purpose, recall, memory and the others start fresh); memoryBlocks frontmatter on custom subagents (specific list, all, or none; default all) sets which memory blocks the child can access; agent_id deploys an existing stateful agent as the subagent (it brings its own memory, not the parent's, and subagent_type must then be general-purpose); background mode changes when the result arrives, not what the child sees
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q4 not answered: the page says the Markdown body 'becomes the subagent's system prompt' but never says whether the child is told it is a subagent. Q1 to Q3 answered. Framework-level agent-to-agent messaging is no longer on a live page: the old multi-agent tutorials (/tutorials/multi-agent/, /tutorials/multi-agent/supervisor-worker/, /tutorials/multi-agent-async/, /guides/agents/multi-agent/, /cookbooks/multi-agent-async) all redirect to the docs home, and the legacy V1 SDK built-in tools page lists only web_search, fetch_webpage and run_code, so no send_message_to_agent tool is documented; the V1 SDK shared-memory page documents coordination only through shared memory blocks ('Agent A writes before handoff, Agent B reads on pickup'). New row.

harnesses.name: OpenCode: subagents in child sessions (v1 docs: Task tool gated by permission.task, subagent_depth, command subtask: true; v2 docs: subagent tool gated by the permissions action subagent, experimental.subagent_depth, command subagent: true)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: the child session starts with fresh context, its own system prompt and the tool-call assignment. v2: 'Subagents run in child sessions with fresh context.' 'A primary agent can invoke one with the subagent tool, either in the foreground or in the background.' v1: subagents are 'specialized assistants that primary agents can invoke for specific tasks' and 'will use the model of the primary agent that invoked the subagent'. Permissions are not inherited either: 'The child currently uses its own configured permissions, not a restricted copy of the parent's permissions.' Returns (commands and migration pages, background child sessions): the parent 'receives the child's result or failure when it finishes'; 'delegated commands now run automatically in the background and report their results to the parent session'.
harnesses.quote: Subagents run in child sessions with fresh context.
harnesses.knob: none documented for context visibility. The documented knobs only gate launching and nesting: v1 permission.task (glob to allow, ask or deny each subagent; 'When set to deny, the subagent is removed from the Task tool description entirely'), v1 subagent_depth (default 1, which 'prevents those subagents from launching additional subagents'), v2 permissions rule with action subagent and the agent ID as resource, v2 experimental.subagent_depth, mode (primary, subagent, all), hidden (removes the agent from 'the subagent catalog advertised to models'), command subtask: true (v1) or subagent: true (v2) to run a command in a child session
harnesses.doc_url: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/agents/ ; https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/ ; https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions/ ; https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/commands/ ; https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/ ; https://opencode.ai/docs/config/ ; https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/ ; https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q4 not answered: no page says what the child is told about being a subagent (v2 only says of the description field 'OpenCode includes it in the subagent catalog shown to the model', which is the parent's view). Q3 answered only on the commands and migration pages (background child sessions report result or failure to the parent); the agents pages describe navigating into child sessions but not the return value. Q1 and Q2 answered. Two doc generations are live in parallel (opencode.ai/docs uses V1 syntax, opencode.ai/v2/docs uses V2); V2 renames the Task tool to the subagent tool, renames the task permission to subagent, and has no scout subagent. New row.

harnesses.name: Goose (goose-docs.ai; block.github.io/goose now redirects there): subagents through the summon platform extension (delegate and load tools; recipes, sub_recipes and custom agents as delegation sources)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: the child runs in its own session with only the delegate call's instructions or source (recipe, subrecipe or custom agent) plus parameters; extensions are inherited. Custom Agents page: 'Delegated subagents run in isolated sessions and do not automatically inherit the full parent conversation.' Subrecipes page: 'Sub-recipe sessions run in isolation - they don't share conversation history, memory, or state with the main recipe or other subrecipes.' The Subagents page is looser ('Internal subagents spawn goose instances to handle tasks using your current session's context and extensions.') but its Default Settings table lists only Extensions as 'Inherited from parent'. Returns: Return Mode defaults to 'Full Details (Default): See all tool executions and reasoning steps' versus 'Summary Only: Get just the final result to keep your conversation clean'; 'If a subagent fails or times out (5-minute default), you will receive no output from that subagent.'; async delegation 'returns a task id' and load(source: task id) 'waits for the result'.
harnesses.quote: s instructions or source (recipe, subrecipe or custom agent) plus parameters; extensions are inherited. Custom Agents page:
harnesses.knob: none documented for passing the parent conversation to the child. What exists: delegate(instructions: ...) or delegate(source: ...) carries the assignment; sub_recipes values pre-set parameters ('Pre-set values take precedence over context-based parameters') while the parent model fills the rest from its own context; load(source: ...) goes the other way (pulls an agent's or recipe's instructions into the current conversation instead of delegating); Return Mode (natural language) and delegate(..., async: true) change what and when the parent gets back; the subagent_system.md prompt template customizes the child's system prompt; GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS and settings.max_turns cap turns
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q4 only half answered: the prompt-templates page lists subagent_system.md as 'System prompt for subagents spawned to handle specific tasks' (so the child runs under a subagent-specific system prompt) but its content is only linked to the GitHub source, not reproduced in the docs. Q1 to Q3 answered. Subagents cannot nest ('Subagent spawning: Cannot create additional subagents to prevent infinite recursion') and are disabled outside autonomous permission mode. New row.

harnesses.name: Windsurf, now Devin Desktop (docs.windsurf.com 307-redirects to docs.devin.ai): Cascade (Fast Context retrieval subagent, workflows, one-click delegation to cloud Devin) and the Devin Local agent's subagents (run_subagent and read_subagent tools, profiles subagent_explore and subagent_general, custom agents/<name>.md profiles)
harnesses.default_visibility: Two agents. Cascade (legacy): no general delegation, 'plugins and subagents have no Cascade equivalent at all'; its only subagent is Fast Context, auto-triggered for retrieval: 'When Cascade receives a query that requires code search, Fast Context will trigger automatically.' What Fast Context receives beyond the query is not stated. Workflows are not delegation: 'Upon invocation, Cascade sequentially processes each step defined in the Workflow'. Cloud Devin gets the plan: 'work on a plan with a local agent and, with a single click, send it to Devin for implementation'. Devin Local (default local agent, same harness as Devin CLI): NONE by documented mechanism. The child gets the parent's prompt, tools and repo, not the transcript: 'A subagent shares tools and codebase context with the parent', it 'operates in its own conversation chain', 'it does not inherit the parent's conversation history'. Background subagents also inherit session tool grants: 'Background subagents inherit any tool permissions you have already granted during the current session.' ask_user_question 'is always withheld from subagents'; run_subagent and read_subagent are disabled inside a subagent unless max-nesting is set.
harnesses.quote: plugins and subagents have no Cascade equivalent at all
harnesses.knob: No knob changes what the child sees of the parent conversation; the parent's prompt is the only channel (a finished subagent 'can be resumed with a new prompt'). Documented switches: subagents_enabled (user config.json; false removes the run_subagent and read_subagent tools), the Subagents (Preview) toggle in Devin Settings, the org Default subagent model setting (Subagent router, a specific model, or None which disables subagents), profile choice by the parent (subagent_explore: read-only plus web search on the default subagent model; subagent_general: full tools in the foreground, pre-approved tools only in the background, parent's model), foreground vs background, and custom profile frontmatter name, description, model, allowed-tools, max-nesting. Cascade side: none documented (Fast Context has no setting on its page; workflows are markdown step lists).
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether a Devin Local subagent is told it is a subagent (built-in profile prompts are not published; the custom-profile example is user-authored text such as 'report findings back to the parent agent'), and what Fast Context receives from Cascade. Returns: 'When a subagent finishes, the parent agent reads the result and summarizes the key findings and actions for you.' 'You do not see the subagent's raw output directly.' Background: 'The parent is automatically notified when the subagent completes.' A subagent moved to the background mid-run: 'The subagent's result won't feed back into the parent's current pipeline'. Fast Context returns 'targeted results'. Cloud Devin returns PRs reviewed in the editor. Quick Review is a separate review subagent that 'analyzes the diff' (Devin Local only). Devin Local is the default for new tabs; Cascade is still selectable.

harnesses.name: JetBrains Junie: Junie CLI custom subagents (.junie/agents/*.md or .agents/*.md with YAML frontmatter, auto-delegated by name and description; no subagent feature is documented for the Junie IDE plugin)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism. The child runs on its own system prompt (the file's prompt body) plus the task the main agent delegates: 'This prompt will be added to the instructions delegated from the main agent.' It does not get the main conversation: 'The subagent then works independently in its own context and returns the result to the main agent.' and subagents keep 'the subagent's context out of the main conversation'. With allowPromptArgument true, 'the delegated user request is appended automatically as User Input' when $prompt is not referenced in the body. The pages never enumerate what 'instructions delegated' contain (task text only, or excerpts of history).
harnesses.quote: s prompt body) plus the task the main agent delegates:
harnesses.knob: allowPromptArgument (exposes $prompt, the delegated user request, to the subagent prompt) and prompt-body variables such as $path and $focus are the only documented context levers; nothing passes the parent transcript. Other frontmatter: tools (allowlist of tool groups Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, WebSearch, AskUserQuestion), disallowedTools, mcpServers, model, reasoningLevel (alias effort), maxTurns, skills, permissionMode (default, acceptEdits, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan). Session policy: /settings then Subagents, SameModelOnly or Auto (default), saved in ~/.junie/settings.json (Early Access).
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether the subagent is told it is a subagent (the user is: 'Junie CLI invokes subagents automatically, informing the user which subagent has started working on the task.'). Returns: the main agent 'runs it as a subtask, and brings the result back into the main session'; subagent transcripts are written to the session's subagents folder (Ctrl+O opens them). Subagents 'cannot be invoked manually via slash commands'. Junie also imports .claude/agents, .cursor/agents and .codex/agents files.

harnesses.name: Replit Agent (Agent 4, current): task system background tasks (each task gets its own Agent and thread in an isolated project copy); no user-facing sub-agent, 'extended thinking' or parallel-agent API is documented on docs.replit.com
harnesses.default_visibility: A selection of state, not the parent conversation by any documented statement: the task worker receives the approved task brief and the project. 'Background tasks are separate threads where Agent works independently in isolated copies of your project.' 'Each task also gets its own Agent and inherits your full project context, so you don't repeat yourself.' Before it starts a task holds 'the task title, description, and plan' (the plan lists scope, implementation steps, definition of done, relevant files, agent mode). Threads: 'each background task gets its own thread' 'so Agent can keep task work isolated without mixing up the conversations.' Whether 'full project context' includes the main-thread transcript is not stated.
harnesses.quote: Background tasks are separate threads where Agent works independently in isolated copies of your project.
harnesses.knob: none documented that changes what the task's Agent sees. Levers that shape the brief: View plan, Revise plan, Accept tasks or Start building, Plan mode task lists; concurrency by plan (Starter none, Core 1, Pro 10, Enterprise 64); dependencies detected by Agent. Effort (Low to Max, per model) and Agent modes (Free, Power, Max) set reasoning and cost, not context. The Agent 3 'Extended Thinking' and 'High Power' toggles no longer appear anywhere on docs.replit.com (site-wide llms-full.txt has no 'extended thinking', 'high power' or 'subagent'); only App Testing's 'Extended Autonomy' and an internal 'parallel multi-agent search' for warehouse queries remain.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. New row. Not answered by the pages: whether the task's Agent is told it is a delegated task, and whether the main thread's conversation is part of 'full project context'. Returns go to the user, not to a parent agent: 'When a task finishes, Agent shows you what it did: the work log, test results, and a live preview of the changes.' You Apply or Dismiss; 'Agent handles conflict resolution automatically when applying changes from multiple tasks.' After apply the main chat carries 'the implementation summary, checks, warnings'. Agent 4 changelog: 'Run tasks in parallel: Agent handles multiple tasks at once so you can move faster'.

harnesses.name: Manus: Wide Research (the main agent decomposes a task into sub-tasks and deploys parallel sub-agents; automatically triggered)
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: each sub-agent starts in a fresh context that holds only its decomposed sub-task (one item), not the parent's conversation: 'Each agent receives its own dedicated context and processes one item independently.' and 'Each sub-task is assigned to a dedicated agent with its own fresh context window'. The parent does the decomposition: 'The main agent analyzes your request and breaks it into independent sub-tasks (e.g., "research company #1", "research company #2", etc.)'. Returns: 'The main agent collects all completed sub-tasks and assembles them into your requested format (table, report, dataset, etc.)'. Scale (help center): 'Wide Research can run 20 subtasks simultaneously, equivalent to having 20 Agents helping with one task.'
harnesses.knob: none documented: no setting changes what a sub-agent sees, and the feature cannot even be invoked by hand: 'This feature only supports automatic triggering.' (help center). The only documented sub-agent control is the model tier: in Manus 1.6 MAX 'all sub-Agents performing "Wide Research" use a more advanced model architecture' (changes the model, not visibility). Each sub-task's credit use is capped at 50 credits.
harnesses.doc_url: https://manus.im/docs/features/wide-research ; https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11960169-what-is-wide-research ; https://manus.im/docs/llms.txt (docs index: no other sub-agent or delegation page)
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q1 (fresh per-item context), Q2 (no knob, automatic trigger only) and Q3 (main agent collects and assembles results) answered; Q4 (whether the sub-agent is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed on either page. The docs index lists no other delegation page (the Manus API page only points to open.manus.im). New row.

harnesses.name: Dify: Agent node in Workflow/Chatflow (classic Agent node: LLM plus Dify tools, including a Workflow published as a tool; new Agent node (beta): invite a published Agent and give it an 'Agent task') and Workflow as Tool
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism. New Agent node: the invited agent receives only the task text written in 'Agent task' (plus upstream variables pulled in with '/', as text, and files): 'There you set only the task you want done.' and 'This is separate from the agent's own prompt and capabilities.'; 'Variables you pull in reach the agent as text and are truncated at 2,000 characters.'; runs are isolated: 'nothing from one node's run (files it wrote, tools it installed) carries into another'. Returns: 'By default, an Agent node returns a single output, text: the agent's reply to its task, as one block of text.' plus declared outputs (files capped at 50 MB). Workflow as Tool (callable from the classic Agent node, Agent apps or another workflow): the child workflow receives only the tool parameters, that is its User Input fields: 'Turn any Workflow that starts with a User Input node into a tool, so you can reuse multi-step logic across apps.'; it returns its Output node variables: 'Each output variable name becomes a key in the tool's result, accessible to the parent workflow that invokes the tool.' The classic Agent node itself sees only its Instruction, its Query ('Query specifies the user input or task the Agent should work on.') and a bounded history window ('Memory controls how many previous messages the Agent remembers using TokenBufferMemory.').
harnesses.knob: New Agent node: the 'Agent task' field (type '/' to pull in outputs from earlier nodes, truncated at 2,000 characters as text; 'To hand over longer content in full, pass it as a file: the agent receives the whole file and reads it in its sandbox.') and 'New output' declarations for what comes back. Classic Agent node: the 'Memory' window (how much prior conversation the agent node sees) and the per-tool parameter mode ('auto-generated' parameters are populated by the Agent, 'manual input' parameters are fixed in the tool configuration), which decides what a called workflow-tool receives. No agent-to-agent handoff or agent-as-tool parameter is documented.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q1, Q2 and Q3 answered for both paths (Agent node and Workflow as Tool); Q4 (whether the invited agent or called workflow is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed. The new Agent node 'is in beta and available in Workflow apps only', so there is no chat history to pass; the classic Agent node page documents tools but no sub-agent feature, and the new Agent's tool types ('plugins, custom APIs, workflows, and MCP servers') include no agent type. New row.

harnesses.name: n8n: AI Agent Tool sub-node (agent as tool, nestable), Call n8n Workflow Tool sub-node (sub-workflow as tool, paired with the Execute Sub-workflow Trigger's Input data mode) and Agents (Preview) Sub-agents
harnesses.default_visibility: NONE by documented mechanism: the child receives only the tool-call input. AI Agent Tool: its own 'Prompt (User Message)' (static text, an expression, or a value the parent model fills through $fromAI()) plus its own 'System Message'; no page passes the parent's conversation or memory sub-node: 'Prompt (User Message): The prompt to the LLM explaining what actions to perform and what information to return.'; 'System Message: A message to send to the agent before the conversation starts.'; 'This allows you to use multiple agents in a single workflow without the complexity of managing context and variables that sub-workflows require.' Call n8n Workflow Tool: the sub-workflow receives only the 'Workflow Inputs' defined by its trigger's schema: 'The Call n8n Workflow Tool node is a tool that allows an agent to run another n8n workflow and fetch its output data.'; model-filled values are drawn from the parent's context: 'The AI model will use the context from the task and information from other connected tools to fill in the appropriate details.' Returns: the sub-agent's final output (intermediate steps only when 'Return Intermediate Steps' is on); for sub-workflows 'The last node of Workflow B sends the data back to the Execute Sub-workflow node in Workflow A.' and 'The error text is returned to the agent as the tool result.' Agents (Preview): 'Sub-agents let this agent hand off work to other published agents.' with no statement of what is handed over.
harnesses.knob: $fromAI(key, description, type, defaultValue) in 'Prompt (User Message)' or in 'Workflow Inputs' (or the 'Let the model define this parameter' button) lets the parent model decide what the child receives; the sub-workflow trigger's 'Input data mode' ('Define using fields below', 'Define using JSON example', 'Accept all data') fixes the input schema; 'Automatically Passthrough Binary Images' forwards binary images to the sub-agent as image messages; 'Return Intermediate Steps' and 'Require Specific Output Format' shape what returns. Agents (Preview): only 'When should this agent be used?' (a delegation description) and a maximum number of sub-agents running in parallel; no context setting.
harnesses.notes: partially_verified. Q2 and Q3 answered; Q1 is answered only by the parameter inventory (the pages list Prompt (User Message) and System Message as the sub-agent's inputs and never state in words that the parent's history or memory is withheld); Q4 (whether the child is told it is orchestrated) is not addressed; for Agents (Preview) Sub-agents the page documents the hand-off but not what is passed. New row.

result.notes: Submission check 2026-09-04: nine harness rows owed since the second web pass (Letta, OpenCode, Goose, Windsurf, Junie, Replit, Manus, Dify, n8n), each from official documentation fetched on 2026-09-04 by a fresh-context agent.
